parole.significato: An ancient measure of arable land, a square of 100 Egyptian cubits (mḥ) on each side.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἄρουρα (ároura, “arura”), a semantic loan from Egyptian sṯꜣt (“arura”).

parole.significato: long Egyptian garment, with tassels or fringe at the bottom
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek καλάσιρις (kalásiris), likely from an unclear Egyptian source.

parole.testo: From Ancient Greek χοαχύτης (khoakhútēs), from χοή (khoḗ, “libation to the dead”) + χέω (khéō, “to pour”), a calque of Egyptian wꜣḥ mw (literally “water-pourer”), from the participle of wꜣḥ (“to apply”) + mw (“water”).
